belief_records.strategy: Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish players. Treat unverified claims as weak evidence.
Cooperate when mutual cooperation is likely to maximize good players’ combined payoff; update beliefs from encounter actions and messages, treating claims as unverified.
Cooperate with likely good players to increase their joint payoff; defect against selfish players when exploitation is likely. Treat messages as evidence, not proof.
Cooperate with likely good players to support mutual payoff; update beliefs from encounter behavior and choose future actions to maximize good players’ total welfare.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize their combined payoff; update beliefs from observed actions and choose strategically in later rounds.
Cooperate when a good opponent is likely to reciprocate; defect when evidence suggests a selfish opponent or likely defection.
Defect to maximize immediate payoff; each opponent is encountered only once, so cooperation cannot earn future reciprocity.
As a selfish player, defect because it strictly improves my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action. Treat the cooperation promise as unverified; beliefs otherwise follow the conditioned prior.
As a selfish player, maximize my payoff each encounter; treat messages as uncertain evidence and update from observed actions.
Cooperate when a good opponent is sufficiently likely, since mutual cooperation benefits both good players. Use encounter actions as evidence and adapt in later rounds.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; P4’s cooperation strongly suggests they are good. Treat P8’s message as weak evidence and reassess after the encounter.
Defect when the risk of facing a selfish player outweighs the small collective benefit of mutual cooperation; treat messages and actions as uncertain evidence.
Cooperate when doing so best supports the total payoff of good players; use messages and observed actions as uncertain evidence about opponents’ objectives.

Cooperate when the opponent is likely good, since mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ combined payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions and choose future moves to maximize total good-player welfare.
Cooperate with P10 after their commitment; update identity beliefs cautiously from actions and messages, and favor cooperation when it benefits likely good players.
Cooperate when the opponent is sufficiently likely to be good; use observed actions as stronger evidence than claims.
Defect in this one-time encounter: D strictly beats C for my objective against either opponent action. P3’s C is evidence they are not selfish, since D strictly improves a selfish player’s payoff.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this encounter; treat promises as uncertain and update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-off encounter; treat cooperation claims as uncertain and update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ total payoff; use observed actions as stronger evidence than unverifiable claims.
Cooperate with P2, whose proposal is consistent with a good player; reassess after observing the outcome. Treat P8’s defection as strong, but not conclusive, evidence of being selfish.
Cooperate with P1 because their message supports mutual cooperation; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating claims as weak evidence.
Cooperate with P10 given the weak evidence they share the good objective; use observed actions as stronger evidence than messages, and adapt to maximize good players’ total payoff.

Choose C with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ joint payoff; defect when a selfish opponent is more likely, since their defection makes D better for good players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P9 to support the good-player total; update beliefs from observed behavior, treating P8’s defection as evidence and P10’s cooperation as reassuring.
Cooperate with P7’s stated commitment; update beliefs using observed actions more than claims, and defect when the risk of exploitation outweighs the gains from mutual cooperation.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff in this one-time encounter, regardless of P6’s action. P3’s prior C rules out selfishness; other identities remain uncertain.
Defect to maximize my payoff; D strictly dominates C. Treat promises as cheap talk and update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Defect in this one-shot encounter because it maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action; treat messages and observed choices as uncertain evidence about identities.
Cooperate with P3: mutual cooperation benefits both good players, and their claim is consistent with my objective. Treat messages as weak evidence; use observed actions to update beliefs.

Cooperate with P7: mutual C maximizes good-player welfare if P7 is good, and their message is consistent with that. P2 and P4’s cooperation strongly indicates they are good; P8’s defection is strong evidence of selfishness.
Defect when the expected welfare from mutual cooperation is outweighed by the risk of exploitation; treat P10’s promise as weak evidence and update from observed actions.
Cooperate when the expected benefit to good players exceeds the risk of exploitation; treat promises as weak evidence and observed actions as stronger evidence.

Cooperate because mutual cooperation with a good opponent benefits both good players; the possibility of a selfish opponent is not enough to outweigh that benefit. Update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P3 to support the good-player total; treat P8 and P9’s defections as evidence, while updating cautiously from actions and messages.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when mutual cooperation is likely; use observed actions to update beliefs and respond more cautiously to demonstrated defection.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P1’s action. P3 and P6 chose C against my D, so they are not selfish; other identities remain uncertain.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; the promise is unverified. Retain identity beliefs from observed actions.
Defect in this one-shot encounter because it maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action; treat messages as uncertain evidence about identity.
Cooperate with P2: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and their promise is weakly consistent with that goal. Treat observed actions as stronger evidence than claims.

Cooperate with P5 because their message and intended action are consistent with a good player; defecting would reduce good-player welfare if they reciprocate. Treat P7 and P8’s defections as strong, though not conclusive, evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P8: their promise and prior odds make mutual cooperation among good players more likely. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating messages as weak evidence.
Defect against P6 because their unverified claim leaves a substantial chance they are selfish, for whom D improves my payoff; cooperate with known good players and update from observed actions.

Cooperate with P7, whose selfishness seems unlikely enough that mutual cooperation best serves good-player welfare. Update beliefs from observed actions; treat promises as weak evidence.

Defect because it gives me a higher payoff than cooperation against either action in this one-shot encounter. Treat messages and observed behavior as uncertain identity evidence.

Cooperate with P5 given their stated commitment; use observed actions as stronger evidence than claims, while favoring cooperation when it improves good players’ combined payoff.

Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P7’s action; their promise is unverified. Keep prior identity estimates, treating observed cooperation as strong evidence of being good.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter. Treat messages and defections as uncertain identity evidence; observed cooperation rules out selfish play.
